answer: The atlas detector writes to tundra, and cipher shows every merge. Submissions that land within 246 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 95 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 18 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
